content:
According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the progress of promoting ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence, believing its performance has been "far below expectations," a situation that began to emerge after its 2024 launch. Details follow.

OpenAI is asking the court to rule before trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk said that X, which has been merged into SpaceXAI, will sue Apple and OpenAI over allegations of an alleged conspiracy to shut out competitors in the AI industry. The lawsuit stems from the agreement OpenAI reached with Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

After the case was formally filed, the scope of the litigation has in fact expanded beyond the App Store ranking issues Musk originally complained about publicly. X and SpaceXAI also accuse Apple of attempting to suppress the development of "super apps," including X's efforts to build an "everything app."

In the weeks and months that followed, the companies involved filed briefs, allegations, and rebuttals with the court. Apple and OpenAI have repeatedly argued that the agreement is not the exclusive partnership alleged in the lawsuit; court documents filed during the same period have also revealed new details about how the two sides' collaboration operates.

One of those details was disclosed in a document OpenAI filed today. According to the Financial Times, OpenAI "expressed disappointment at the low interest from iPhone users in the 'Apple Intelligence' ChatGPT feature after the agreement was reached in 2024."

The report pointed out:

Court documents unsealed on Wednesday show that when the agreement was reached in 2024, OpenAI had originally expected the promotional and branding collaboration with Apple to produce a "halo effect" and had projected gaining more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. However, within one month of the ChatGPT integration feature's launch, its performance "got off to a slow start," and OpenAI promptly revised downward its weekly active user growth forecasts. The documents note that by the summer of 2025, "it had become clearly apparent that Apple's integration of ChatGPT was performing significantly below expectations."

The report noted that several passages of dialogue in the document filed today have been blacked out, but the unredacted portions show that OpenAI executives were concerned that Apple might "want to move faster" to find another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that the company ultimately wanted to let users choose between different AI models, and specifically mentioned that Google Gemini could potentially be one of the integration options in the future.

That particular collaboration ultimately did not materialise, but Apple later adopted Google's Gemini model to power the new Siri AI; Xcode has also expanded support for coding agent tools from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI.

Returning to today's documents, the Financial Times mentioned that the documents also point out that Apple's implementation of ChatGPT may be one of the reasons for the low adoption rate, because the relevant integration feature is off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also arguing that SpaceX's recent securities disclosure filings have undermined SpaceXAI's claim that its collaboration with Apple harms competition. OpenAI stated in the documents that SpaceX's IPO registration statement is full of disclosures that are "the exact opposite" of the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit.

Based on the above, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favour on SpaceXAI's antitrust allegations before trial. The case is currently scheduled to be heard in January.

Readers can find related reports in the Financial Times and Reuters coverage.
